svg.title: Checkpointing versus offload
svg.desc: Compares activation checkpointing and activation offload across memory and recomputation paths.
svg.text: Activation checkpointing vs activation offload
Checkpointing recomputes; offload moves tensors to another storage tier. Both reduce peak GPU memory in different ways.
Forward pass with checkpoints
Block 1 -> Block 2 -> Block 3 -> Block 4
keep only selected checkpoint states, drop intermediate activations
Checkpointing
• save fewer activations
• backward re-runs the local forward segment
• trades compute for memory
• best for long blocks with expensive activation storage
Offload
• move activations to CPU / pinned memory / slower tier
• backward fetches them back when needed
• trades transfer for memory
• best when recomputation is too expensive
What to remember
1. checkpointing: keep fewer states, recompute on backward.
2. offload: keep states, but move them to another storage tier.
3. both exist to reduce GPU peak memory; they are not the same optimization.
4. the page should make the tradeoff visible before the code does.
5. offload and checkpointing can be combined with other memory strategies.
